content:
Im currently upgrading my repo by 4 versions at once and i realize i'm spending most of the time scrolling to the first file with an (x) in the error message and then spend time opening up that file and scrolling to the error location.
It would be really useful if somewhere in the message there was a link which would take me to the correct file (or even the exact location already)
Well, then it would also be useful for the interactive window :yum:
For example, open a terminal in VS Code, type lake build there --- errors come with file and line information, so you can alt-click to jump to the location.

Interactive: you can use F8 and F9 to jump to the next warning/resp error. (If parts of a file are still elaborating ("you see orange bars next to it", any errors/warnings those will cause are not seen, of course.) This works across all your open files, by the way.

If i open an interactive file which imports an (unopened) erroring file, the error has the wrong location in vscode, so F8 doesn't take me to the actual problem (i just stay in the currently opened file)
But within that file, you get good location information, right?
That's strange and looks like a bug/something to improve to me!
The problem with the F8 approach is, that vscode only shows errors in already opened files.

Michael Rothgang said:

open a terminal in VS Code, type lake build there --- errors come with file and line information, so you can alt-click to jump to the location.

I only learned this quite recently, and it's been really helpful!
